cases.sentence: Дарья Александровна хотела сказать свои мысли ___, но почему-то ей теперь это показалось не у места.
cases.explain: «нынешнего утра» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Darya Alexandrovna wanted to express her thoughts of the morning, but for some reason it seemed to her now out of place to do so.

cases.sentence: – Я полагаю… – начала было Дарья Александровна, но в это время Васенька Весловский, наладив коба на галоп с ___, грузно шлепаясь в своей коротенькой жакетке о замшу дамского седла, прогалопировал мимо них.
cases.explain: «правой ноги» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I consider. …” Darya Alexandrovna was beginning, but at that instant Vassenka Veslovsky, having brought the cob to gallop with the right leg foremost, galloped past them, bumping heavily up and down in his short jacket on the chamois leather of the side saddle. “He’s doing it, Anna Arkadyevna!” he shouted.

cases.sentence: Анна даже и не взглянула на него; но опять Дарье Александровне показалось, что в коляске неудобно начинать этот ___, и потому она сократила свою мысль.
cases.explain: «длинный разговор» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Anna did not even glance at him; but again it seemed to Darya Alexandrovna out of place to enter upon such a long conversation in the carriage, and so she cut short her thought.

cases.sentence: Анна, отведя глаза от лица друга и сощурившись (это была ___, которой не знала за ней Долли), задумалась, желая вполне понять значение этих слов.
cases.explain: «новая привычка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Anna, taking her eyes off her friend’s face and dropping her eyelids (this was a new habit Dolly had not seen in her before), pondered, trying to penetrate the full significance of the words. And obviously interpreting them as she would have wished, she glanced at Dolly.

cases.explain: «богатая натура» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “These are the servants’ houses, barns, and stables,” answered Anna. “And there the park begins. It had all gone to ruin, but Alexey had everything renewed. He is very fond of this place, and, what I never expected, he has become intensely interested in looking after it. But his is such a rich nature! Whatever he takes up, he does splendidly. So far from being bored by it, he works with passionate interest. He—with his temperament as I know it—he has become careful and businesslike, a first-rate manager, he positively reckons every penny in his management of the land. But only in that. When it’s a question of tens of thousands, he doesn’t think of money.” She spoke with that gleefully sly smile with which women often talk of the secret characteristics only known to them—of those they love. “Do you see that big building? that’s the new hospital. I believe it will cost over a hundred thousand; that’s his hobby just now. And do you know how it all came about? The peasants asked him for some meadowland, I think it was, at a cheaper rate, and he refused, and I accused him of being miserly. Of course it was not really because of that, but everything together, he began this hospital to prove, do you see, that he was not miserly about money. C’est une petitesse, if you like, but I love him all the more for it. And now you’ll see the house in a moment. It was his grandfather’s house, and he has had nothing changed outside.”

cases.sentence: Это еще ___, и он ничего не изменен снаружи.
cases.explain: «дедовский дом» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: – Как хорош! – сказала Долли, с невольным удивлением глядя на прекрасный с колоннами дом, выступающий из разноцветной зелени ___ сада.
cases.explain: «старых деревьев» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “How beautiful!” said Dolly, looking with involuntary admiration at the handsome house with columns, standing out among the different-colored greens of the old trees in the garden.

cases.sentence: Они въехали в усыпанный щебнем и убранный цветником двор, на котором два работника обкладывали взрыхленную цветочную клумбу необделанными ноздреватыми камнями, и остановились в ___.
cases.explain: «крытом подъезде» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: They drove into a courtyard strewn with gravel and bright with flowers, in which two laborers were at work putting an edging of stones round the light mould of a flower bed, and drew up in a covered entry.

cases.sentence: – А, они уже приехали! – сказала Анна, глядя на ___, которых только что отводили от крыльца. – Не правда ли, хороша эта лошадь?
cases.explain: «верховых лошадей» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Ah, they’re here already!” said Anna, looking at the saddle horses, which were just being led away from the steps. “It is a nice horse, isn’t it? It’s my cob; my favorite. Lead him here and bring me some sugar. Where is the count?” she inquired of two smart footmen who darted out. “Ah, there he is!” she said, seeing Vronsky coming to meet her with Veslovsky.

cases.sentence: – Pardon, j'en ai tout plein les poches, – улыбаясь, отвечал он, опуская пальцы в ___.
cases.explain: «жилетный карман» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Pardon, j’en ai tout plein les poches,” he answered, smiling, putting his fingers in his waistcoat pocket.
